title: Reclassify global default set: move project-specific skills out of global
description:
Currently all 78 canonical skills are globally deployed by default. Per the scoping design (docs/scoping-rationale.md), the global set should contain only the TRULY UNIVERSAL skills — everything else becomes project-add-only.

Obvious candidates to move OUT of global (into project-add territory):
- cbm (codebase intelligence — only wanted in code projects)
- shopping-management, ticket-management, ticket-audit, ticket-find, filing-process, etc. (personal/workflow skills not relevant to code work)
- use-railway (deployment context, project-specific)
- Any code-specific skill that shouldn't trigger in non-code sessions

The mechanism ships first (skills-81s) with global-manifest.toml listing everything, so behaviour is unchanged. THIS ticket then curates global-manifest.toml down to the universal core, incrementally — no need to get it perfect in one pass.

Process: for each skill, ask 'would I want this in every session regardless of project?' If no, remove from global-manifest.toml. It remains canonical and available via project add/exclude.

This is governance work, not code — but it's the bulk of making scoping actually useful. Without it, the global set stays bloated and the project-add mechanism has little to add.

title: Skill quality control: naming convention, linting, and description-driven loading
description: Skill naming is inconsistent and unenforced. Survey of the 81-skill set: object-verb (skills-manage, change-manage, work-unit-manage, location-manage, project-manage, git-change-manage, jj-change-manage - 7 in one family) coexists with verb-object (write-design-doc, update-docs, use-railway), noun-agent (discovery-architect, documentation-writer, go-slice-planner, bin-creator), and bare verbs (plan, verify, wrap, orientate, retro). Near-duplicate concepts exist (documentation-writer AND documentation-writing; four overlapping change-management skills). No convention is documented or enforced. THREE related gaps in priority order. (1) AUTO-LOADING via description quality: a skill only helps if it loads at the right moment; descriptions must be strong enough to trigger reliably (skills-manage should auto-load before ANY skill authoring, not wait to be remembered). A skill that is not loaded is invisible - this is the highest-impact gap. (2) LINTING: enforce naming convention, frontmatter schema, description quality, and duplicate-concept detection as a deploy/reconcile check. Likely existing tools (skillkit is half-present; community skill-linters exist). (3) EVALS: no way to test a skill improves agent behavior or loads in the right contexts. All three are one root problem: skills authored by hand with no quality gate between authoring and deploy. This issue scopes the work, does not solve it now.

title: Warn on deploy when canonical skills are absent from global-manifest.toml
description:
Footgun surfaced while deploying skills-manage: adding a skill to canonical does NOT automatically add it to global-manifest.toml, so it silently won't deploy. Since deploy reads the manifest (not canonical directly) to determine the global set, a new skill is invisible until the manifest is manually edited.

This is inherent to the explicit-manifest design (reclassification ticket skills-2gs relies on the manifest being curated deliberately), but it's a real footgun for rapid skill creation — you author a skill, deploy, and wonder why it's missing.

Fix: deploy should warn when canonical contains skills not present in global-manifest.toml. The warning should:
- Fire at the start of a global deploy (not project deploy — projects use add/exclude)
- List the canonical skills missing from the manifest
- Suggest adding them to global-manifest.toml (or note they're available only via project add, which may be intentional)
- Be a WARNING, not an error — deploy should still proceed (the manifest is authoritative for what's global; missing skills may be deliberately project-add-only)

This pairs with the reclassification effort: once global-manifest is curated down (skills-2gs), MOST canonical skills will legitimately be absent from global and this warning would fire constantly. So the warning should probably distinguish 'recently added and likely forgotten' from 'deliberately not global'. Simplest heuristic: only warn if the skill was added to canonical recently (e.g. mtime within last N days) AND is absent from manifest. Or: make it informational (--strict flag to promote to error). Decide on the shape during implementation.

Related: the manifest header already has a NOTE about this friction (added in the drift-prevention commit).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 819de03. Global deploy warns when canonical has skills absent from global-manifest.toml; --strict promotes to error (exit 1). Project scope exempt. Tested all scenarios.

title: AGENTS.md instruction files are unmanaged — no source of truth, drift risk
description:
Surfaced during skills-management work. The always-loaded instruction files — ~/.agents/AGENTS.md (opencode family) and ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (Codex) — are currently hand-maintained with no source of truth, no version control, and no deploy mechanism. They contain substantial content (tool-selection guidance, Nia workflow, RTK commands, codebase-memory priority order) that lives only on this machine.

This is a parallel problem to the skills drift we just solved: these files are high-leverage (loaded every session, reach every agent before any skill) but completely unmanaged. If this machine died, they'd be gone.

The skills-manage effort needs to add a small note to these files (skills authoring location + pointer to skills-manage skill), which makes the unmanaged-ness acute: we're about to inject canonical-store metadata into files that have no canonical home of their own.

Scope of the real problem (separate effort):
- Where do AGENTS.md files get authored? (A dir in Dotfiles? A new canonical store? Per-harness variants?)
- How do they deploy? (symlink from Dotfiles already does this for some — ~/.config/opencode is symlinked — but ~/.codex/AGENTS.md and ~/.agents/AGENTS.md are plain files)
- How are per-harness differences handled? (Codex AGENTS.md has RTK/codebase-memory content; opencode has tool-selection/Nia — they're not identical)
- Version control?

Out of scope for skills-manage but flagged here so it's tracked. The skills-manage note will be hand-added to AGENTS.md for now, accepting the unmanaged-ness as a known cost.

title: Implement project-scoping: --dest flag + manifest resolution
description:
Extend skills-deploy with two-scope deployment per docs/scoping-rationale.md.

Scope 1 — global (already works, needs the manifest):
- Read repos/skills/global-manifest.toml (list of canonical skill names that ship by default)
- skills-deploy deploy mirrors ONLY that set to ~/.agents/skills + ~/.codex/skills (currently mirrors everything)

Scope 2 — project (new):
- Add --dest <project-dir> flag
- Read <project-dir>/.agents/skills-manifest.toml (add + exclude fields)
- Resolve: (global_default - exclude) + add
- Mirror resolved set into <project-dir>/.agents/skills/ AND <project-dir>/.codex/skills/ if it exists
- Same mirror semantics: remove skills not in resolved set (with backup), skip symlinks/.system

Manifest format documented in docs/scoping-rationale.md.
Start with global-manifest.toml listing ALL current skills (so behaviour is unchanged until the reclassification ticket runs).

Key constraints:
- One manifest per scope, fanned to all harness dirs at that scope (no per-harness manifests)
- Project skills dir cleaned via mirror, not just appended
- No per-skill frontmatter flags (rejected — see rationale doc)

See docs/scoping-rationale.md for the full design and rejected alternatives.
close_reason:
Implemented in commit eeb28e3.

Two-scope deploy working:
- Global: reads global-manifest.toml (seeded with all 78 skills → behaviour unchanged baseline)
- Project: --dest flag reads <proj>/.agents/skills-manifest.toml, resolves (global - exclude) + add

Tested:
- Global idempotency intact (156 unchanged, 0 writes on re-run)
- Exclude verified: 78 - 3 excluded = 75 deployed to project
- Add verified: (br,almanac,plan - almanac) + cbm,zcode = 4 resolved
- Edge cases: missing manifest (bare global), typo in add (filtered), missing dirs (created), bad --dest (clean error)

global-manifest.toml seeded with all skills per ticket scope; reclassification deferred to skills-2gs (now unblocked).

title: Add 'update' subcommand to skills-deploy for refreshing vendored skills
description:
skills-deploy fetch records url+commit in SOURCES.toml but has no way to pull upstream updates for an already-vendored skill. A natural complement:

  ./deploy/skills-deploy update <name>   # re-fetch latest, update commit pin in SOURCES.toml

Implementation: read existing SOURCES.toml entry for url, git clone --depth 1, diff against current vendor/<name>/, rsync if changed, update commit pin. Low priority — vendored skills don't change often, and manual re-fetch works in the meantime.

title: Verify provenance for vendored skills with UNKNOWN source
description:
Five vendored skills were gathered as-is because their upstream repos were uncertain. They are marked UNKNOWN in SOURCES.toml and need their real upstream identified, then re-fetched via 'skills-deploy fetch' so SOURCES.toml records the correct url + commit.

Skills to verify:
- article-extractor (third-party.md said 'PAI/skillfish community' — generic Readability wrapper)
- tapestry (third-party.md said 'PAI community (possibly)' — orchestrates youtube-transcript + article-extractor + ship-learn-next)
- logseq-markdown (third-party.md said jluo41/tools, but that repo has no skill by that name — provenance was stale/wrong)
- total-recall (contextify.sh commercial product; skill is a thin wrapper pointing at https://contextify.sh)
- use-railway (has railway scripts, no confirmed public upstream repo)

For each: find the real upstream, run './deploy/skills-deploy fetch <owner/repo>', verify the fetched SKILL.md matches the gathered one, then remove the old unverified copy from vendor/. Update SOURCES.toml so no UNKNOWN entries remain.

title: skill-creator references missing template files in Codex (subfolder copy bug?)
description:
Another agent used the skill-creator skill to scaffold a new skill, but it failed because skill-creator references template files that are not present in the Codex deployment.

HYPOTHESIS: skills-deploy is not copying subfolders (references/, templates/) within a skill folder — only SKILL.md and top-level files. If so, this is a regression affecting ALL skills that ship auxiliary subdirectories, not just skill-creator.

TO INVESTIGATE:
1. Is skill-creator a Codex .system built-in (out of deploy scope) or a deployed skill? (Earlier audit showed .system/skill-creator/ exists — if so, this isn't a deploy issue at all, it's a Codex packaging problem.)
2. If deploy IS responsible: verify whether rsync in cmd_deploy copies subdirs. Check skills known to have subdirs (use-railway/scripts/, csv-data-summarizer/examples/, supervisor/references/) — are those subdirs present in ~/.codex/skills/ and ~/.agents/skills/ after deploy?
3. The rsync command is 'rsync -aL' which SHOULD copy recursively — '-a' includes -r. So if subdirs are missing, the cause is likely upstream (the canonical source lacks them) not the copy step.

This is potentially serious: if subfolders aren't deploying, many skills are silently broken (supervisor references, use-railway scripts, csv examples, pharmaceutical chisholm/intralign, etc.).
close_reason:
Investigated. Original skill-creator report is a Codex .system packaging issue, out of skills-deploy scope (skill-creator is a built-in we don't deploy; its templates are present in .system/). Subfolder copy verified working.

Separate real bug found and fixed in this ticket: .git dirs from vendored skills leaked into deployments. Added .git to STRIP_EXCLUDES, cleaned csv-data-summarizer + nia .git from vendor sources and all deployed targets. Commit 24fdb5e.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION COMPLETE. Findings:

1. ORIGINAL REPORT IS NOT A SKILLS-DEPLOY BUG. skill-creator is a Codex .system built-in (~/.codex/skills/.system/skill-creator/), NOT deployed by us. It's not in canonical, not in either target. Its templates ARE present in .system/skill-creator/{assets,references,scripts}/. Whatever the other agent hit is a Codex packaging/runtime problem, out of our scope.

2. SUBFOLDER COPY WORKS CORRECTLY. The ticket's hypothesis (deploy not copying references/templates/scripts) is DISPROVEN. Verified use-railway deploys all 18 files (references/ + scripts/) identically to canonical; supervisor keeps references/ + agents/. rsync -a includes -r, recursion is fine.

3. SEPARATE REAL BUG FOUND: .git directories leak into deployments. Vendored skills csv-data-summarizer and nia were fetched via 'git clone' and their .git/ dirs shipped into both targets because STRIP_EXCLUDES only strips .skillkit.json/.skillfish.json/.DS_Store, not .git. This bloats deployments and makes them look like nested git repos. Fixing separately.
